newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Chirac sees counterbalance to EU central bank.
newsitem.headline: Chirac sees counterbalance to EU central bank.

text.p: French President Jacques Chirac said on Saturday that a council of ministers and head of state of countries inside monetary union would act as a political counterbalance to a European central bank.
He also said that the mumber of countries in a single currency at the start would be "significantly more than is thought".

He told a news conference at the end of a two-day summit of EU leaders that "the development of a political power opposite the monetary authorities" was one of the things that remained to be resolved for the single currency.
He said there was agreement on this, although ministers have said a call by France for a political power to oversee European monetary union had not been discussed in Dublin.

"In a form which has yet to be determined, the council of ministers and the council of heads of state and government of the countries which are in the euro will constitute this body of authority opposite the central bank," he said.

France has insisted that while the future independent European central bank will control monetary policy, economic policies, including exchange rate policies, will remain firmly in the hands of elected politicians.
Chirac also said that he saw nothing now which could throw into doubt the launch of a single currency.
And, he said, if one were to ask how many countries would join the single currency when it is first launched in 1999, "there will be significantly more than was thought, than is thought".
